measured_referent.bound_semantics: the fabrication lands iff the descendant write reaches the captured stdout pipe before the signature tail flush — write position inside the gap. Effective write position = nominal offset + ~2.5ms fork/exec+sleep latency (r68 measured), so at offset 80 the write sits ~82.5ms: inside every gap >= 100 cell (margin >= ~17ms vs ~1ms jitter) and outside the 50ms cell. Post-tail ground truth is byte order — the intact signature line + standalone ERROR line — never write_ppid, whose flip lags process teardown (a post-tail write can still sample write_ppid==godot_pid); pre-death is proven the other direction: a splice at gap >= 100 means the child was still inside delay_msec when the write landed

bounded_claim: the midlineforge fabrication-window bound is gap-relative, not an absolute write-latency constant: at a fixed 80ms write offset the splice lands exactly on the cells whose signature gap exceeds the write position (measured: fabricated at {100,200,400,800}, missed at 50 with the intact signature proving the post-tail write), and the crossed cells (offset>198 inside the gap) fabricate too — refuting any absolute edge below ~602ms; the bound's referent is the gap — write position < tail flush — on Linux headless Godot 4.7.2 POSIX pipe semantics only
